summary.text: A gemstone is a piece of mineral crystal cut or polished to make jewelry or other adornments, though some rocks and organic materials such as amber and pearl also count.
The traditional Western split between precious and semi-precious stones goes back to the ancient Greeks, and today emerald, ruby, sapphire and diamond are the precious ones.
That label reflected ancient rarity and quality, not necessarily today's value, so a green garnet can be worth far more than a mid-quality emerald.

facts.label: Diamond grading system
facts.value: Developed by the GIA in the early 1950s

items.prompt: Ruby and sapphire are both the mineral species corundum. What separates the two names?

options.label: Colour: red is ruby, any other colour sapphire
Hardness: ruby is the harder of the two
Origin: they come from different countries
Clarity: sapphire has far fewer flaws

items.explain: Ruby is the red variety of corundum, and corundum of any other colour is considered sapphire.

items.prompt: Amethyst was ranked a precious stone from ancient Greece onward, then lost that status. What most likely caused the change?

options.label: It was found to fade in sunlight
Large deposits were found in Brazil
It turned out to be a kind of glass
It proved too soft for rings

items.explain: Amethyst counted as precious until bulk amethyst was discovered in Brazil in the 19th century, which points to rarity shaping the label.

items.prompt: A freshly mined, rough diamond does not sparkle at all. Why not?

options.label: It is full of inclusions that block light
Its colour is still too dark to shine
It has not been shaped to split and return light
It only sparkles after years of polishing by water

items.explain: Sparkle comes from breaking light into colours and delivering it to the eye, which a rough diamond cannot do until it is properly fashioned, or cut.

items.prompt: Why are soft minerals rarely chosen as gemstones?

options.label: They are too heavy to wear comfortably
They cannot be polished at all
They are never found as crystals
They are brittle and do not last

items.explain: Soft minerals are generally not used as gemstones because of their brittleness and lack of durability.

items.prompt: A seller says any emerald must be worth more than any garnet, because emerald is 'precious' and garnet is not. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, precious stones always cost more
Yes, because emeralds are much harder
No, a green garnet can top a mid-quality emerald
No, garnets are always worth more than emeralds

items.explain: The traditional label does not necessarily reflect modern value: the green garnet tsavorite can be far more valuable than a mid-quality emerald.

items.prompt: For a coloured gem such as a sapphire, what is the main thing that decides its quality?

options.label: How heavy the stone is
How pure and beautiful its colour is
How many facets it was given
How hard it scores on the Mohs scale

items.explain: In gemstones that have colour, the purity and beauty of that colour is the primary determinant of quality.
